To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the prevalence of mental disorders in the population of Russia has decreased by more than 50%, the incidence has increased by more than 20%, the suicide rate has increased by more 20% and the level of disability has decreased by more 20%

the dynamics of mental morbidity and suicide rates in the population of Russia in 1992–2010 years are largely determined by the dynamics of social and economic factors, which is confirmed by the results of regression models.

the dynamics of mental disorders in the Russian Federation population in 1992–2010 years are largely determined by the changes in the health-demographic factors (decreasing birth rates, increasing mortality, aging of the population, etc.) and social-economic factors (decreasing income, unemployment, etc.).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the social-economic factors and their impact on the mental health of the Russian population.
the analysis of the impact of the social-economic factors on the main mental health indicators.
the study of the impact of the social and economic changes in the country on mental health.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Russian Federation is a country where the mental health of the population is deteriorating.
mental health in the Russian population is deteriorating.

the mental health of the population of the country has been deteriorated over the past 18 years, and that this is due to the negative impact of the social-economic factors on the health of the population, and also to the insufficient level of health care and social support.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mental health of the Russian population is determined by a complex of social and economic factors and the state policy in the health care system.
the dynamics of mental disorders in Russia in the 1990s was determined by social and economic changes in the country.

the dynamics of the key indicators of the mental health of the population in Russia is largely determined by changes in health-demographic factors and the level of social-economic development of the country.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamics of mental disorders in the Russian population in the period of social and economic crisis is determined by the changes in the health-demographic indicators and living conditions.

the mental health in the population of Russia is closely related to the social and economic changes and living conditions, and the development of a mental health care system should take into account the social changes and the living conditions in Russia.
the mental health in the country is closely related to the economic situation and the level of life expectancy, which is a key indicator of the social and economic development of the country.
